definitions.explanation: A humble way to refer to one's own husband when speaking to others. This is the traditional term used when women speak about their own husbands.
The master or owner of a household, business, or establishment.

examples.japanese: {主人|しゅじん}は{会社|かいしゃ}です。
{主人|しゅじん}は{今|いま}{会社|かいしゃ}にいます。
examples.english: My husband is at the company now.

examples.japanese: うちの{主人|しゅじん}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.english: My husband is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {主人|しゅじん}がお{世話|せわ}になっております。
examples.english: Thank you for taking care of my husband.

examples.japanese: {主人|しゅじん}と{相談|そうだん}してから、お{返事|へんじ}します。{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ちください。
examples.english: I will reply after consulting with my husband. Please wait a moment.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}の{主人|しゅじん}に{聞|き}く。
この{店|みせ}の{主人|しゅじん}はとても{親切|しんせつ}です。
examples.english: The owner of this shop is very kind.

examples.japanese: {旅館|りょかん}の{主人|しゅじん}が{案内|あんない}してくれました。
examples.english: The owner of the inn showed us around.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}は{主人|しゅじん}をよく{覚|おぼ}えています。
あの{店|みせ}は{主人|しゅじん}が{代|か}わってから、{味|あじ}が{変|か}わりました。{前|まえ}の{方|ほう}がおいしかったです。
examples.english: That shop's taste changed after the owner changed. It was more delicious before.

notes: {主人|しゅじん} is a humble term traditionally used by wives to refer to their own husbands. Some modern Japanese women prefer using {夫|おっと} instead, as {主人|しゅじん} literally means 'master' and can feel hierarchical. When referring to someone else's husband, use ご{主人|しゅじん}. The term can also mean the owner or proprietor of a business.
